name: Board
describe: A grid on the floor: take turns placing or moving pieces by the game's own legal and winner rules; refusals with a reason; bots
examples: a giant four in a row on the floor
take turns placing pieces on a grid
move your pieces across a board and capture
a tic-tac-toe or reversi table with friends

rows.description: Cells deep (row 0 is at the end rowZero names)

rowZero.description: Which end of the board row 0 is, where dropped pieces gather. back: the -z end (in a 3D game the far side from the first seat; seen from above, the top of the screen). front: the +z end (seen from above, the bottom of the screen, as a four-in-a-row board stands)

seatSides.description: The sides of the board the seats stand on, in seat order (letters s, n, e, w; s is +z, the bottom of the screen from above); several seats on one side spread along it. Empty: s and n for two, then e and w

cell.description: Cell size in metres (it shrinks so the board and its seats fit the play area)

at.description: Where the middle of the board is: "centre", a world zone name, or [x, z]

input.description: What acting on a cell means. place: put a piece on that cell. drop: put a piece in that column, it slides to the free cell nearest row 0. move: pick one of your pieces, then where it goes

presence.description: How a player is at the board. walk: your body walks beside and on it and the cell under your feet is yours to act on. cursor: your body stands at your side of the board and you move a mark in your colour (mouse, keys, stick); friends see the mark move

action.description: The input that acts on your cell (walk); with a cursor both the click and interact act

piece.description: The shape of a piece, drawn by the kit in its owner's colour (kind 1 and up are drawn taller)

pieceSize.description: A piece's width as a share of the cell

cellShape.description: Square tiles, or round holes on the slab

turnSeconds.description: Seconds a turn may take before the host plays a move for that player (0: no limit). The simple default until the session flow owns turns

botThink.description: Seconds a bot waits before it moves

endDelay.description: Seconds the finished board stays up before the results

score.description: win: the winner gets 1. pieces: your score is your pieces on the board, as it changes. none: the rules score

endsRound.description: A won or drawn board ends the round

clear.description: World props within this many metres of the board are taken away (walls, doors and ceilings stay); 0 keeps them

seats.description: At round start each player stands at their own side of the board, facing it

edgeReach.description: Walking: how far off the board's edge you can stand and still act on the nearest edge cell (m)

hints.description: Show the mover which cells are legal

soundPlace.description: Sound id when a piece lands

soundRefuse.description: Sound id when a move is refused

soundWin.description: Sound id when the board is won

soundSelect.description: Sound id when a piece is picked

textTheirTurn.description: Goal line on another player's turn ({name})

textNotYourTurn.description: Refusal when it is not your turn

events.name: onMove
events.when: a legal move was played (auto: the turn ran out and the host played it)

events.name: onRefuse
events.when: a move was refused: not legal, or not that player's turn

events.name: onEnd
events.when: the board was won or drawn (the round ends after endDelay)

events.name: onTurn
events.when: the turn passed to a seat

host.how: the host owns the grid, the turn and the result; a copy sends its move and is told why when it is refused; a cursor mark is its own player's

fields.g: the grid, one letter a cell from row 0 ("." empty; read it with board.state.at(c, r), never by hand)
fields.t: the seat whose turn it is
fields.l: [from, to] cell indexes of the last move (-1: none)
fields.b: a 1 per seat that is a bot
fields.w: null, or the result { s: winning seats, c: cells, r: reason, d: 1 for a draw }
fields.d: the round second the turn runs out (0: untimed)

owns.why: interact acts on the cell under the player's feet (params.action)
a won or drawn board ends the round (params.endsRound)
a cursor in place of a body

asks.why: on a board each player is a character walking beside it (presence walk) or a mark that moves over the cells (presence cursor)

lines: Give the rules once, in setup: board.rules({ legal(move, s) → true or the reason in words, winner(s) → null | { seat, cells } | { draw: true } }). The board does turns, refusals, pieces, the win line, bots and the end of the round.

A move is { type: "place", to: [c, r] } or { type: "move", from, to }. s has at, empty, owner, set, line, flank, reach, dropRow, count, full, last, turn, data. apply(move, s) for captures, start(s) for the opening (README.md).

input "place" | "drop" (a column, it slides) | "move". presence "walk" (bodies on the board) or "cursor" (bodies stand at the table, each player moves a mark): the ledger's body line decides it (asked only when the person's words leave it open).

stub.worked: board.rules({ legal: (m, s) => s.empty(...m.to) || 'That cell is taken', winner: s => { const l = s.last && s.line(...s.last, 3); return l ? { seat: s.owner(...s.last), cells: l } : s.full() ? { draw: true } : null; } });
traps: legal and winner run on every copy and in the bot's look ahead: read only the state they are handed, change nothing in them
bots already play (and the turn timer plays for an idle player): add bot(ctx, p, dt) { board.bot(p, dt); } to the hooks only so a bot walks to its cell first
the board ends the round and scores the winner (params.score, endsRound): leave check() returning null, or it ends twice
